newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber closes limit down as supplies pile up.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber closes limit down as supplies pile up.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed the $10.00 limit per thousand board feet down on most contracts amid growing sentiment that prices must fall to generate some demand, dealers said.

"The distribution network is extremely full right now and it is becoming more and more clear that prices are going to have to come down to generate any buying interest," said Neil Schmaedick, analyst with Smith Barney Forest Products.
He noted that cash trade had been slow for three or four weeks.
Dealers also said there may have been selling linked to the absence of major damage to properties in the southeast U.S. from Hurricane Danny.
"It is pretty clear that we didn't get a lot of structural damage and it should have very little impact (on lumber demand in the southeast U.S.)," Schmaedick said.
Floor sources said Cargill Investor Services were a featured seller of September and Refco of November. September closed the $10 per tbf limit down at $351.00.
